modules.title: Cloud and Azure foundations
modules.tagline: What cloud really is, how Azure is organised, and how to never be surprised by a bill.
modules.description: Start with the vocabulary every Azure conversation uses: service models, regions, subscriptions, resource groups, Azure Resource Manager, pricing and SLAs. By the end you can read any Azure architecture diagram and sketch how a React front end, a Node API and a SQL database land on Azure.

lessons.title: Why cloud, and why Azure
lessons.summary: On-premises versus cloud, CapEx versus OpEx, elasticity, and where Azure fits among the big three.
objectives: Explain the business case for cloud in one minute
Describe elasticity, pay-as-you-go and economies of scale
Say why a Microsoft-heavy organisation usually lands on Azure

lessons.title: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS and serverless
lessons.summary: The service models, the shared responsibility line, and where a React app, a Node API and SQL Server sit on it.
objectives: Place any Azure service on the IaaS / PaaS / SaaS / serverless spectrum
Draw the shared responsibility line for each model
Choose a model for a given team and workload

lessons.title: Azure's global footprint
lessons.summary: Geographies, regions, region pairs and availability zones, and how they decide latency, resilience and data residency.
objectives: Tell apart a geography, a region, a region pair and an availability zone
Pick a region for a workload using latency, residency, price and service availability
Explain what zone-redundant means to a stakeholder

lessons.title: How Azure is organised
lessons.summary: Tenant, management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources - the hierarchy that governs cost, access and policy.
objectives: Draw the Azure scope hierarchy from memory
Decide what goes in a subscription versus a resource group
Apply a naming and tagging convention a team can live with

lessons.title: Azure Resource Manager and how you talk to Azure
lessons.summary: Portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs, Bicep and the REST API all go through one front door: Azure Resource Manager.
objectives: Describe what Azure Resource Manager does with every request
Choose between portal, CLI and infrastructure as code for a task
Explain control plane versus data plane and why it matters for security

lessons.title: Pricing, cost and the free tier
lessons.summary: Pay-as-you-go, reservations and savings plans, the pricing calculator, budgets and alerts - the toolkit for a bill with no surprises.
objectives: List what you pay for in a typical web workload
Use budgets, alerts and tags to keep cost visible
Explain reservations and savings plans and when they are worth it

lessons.title: SLAs, reliability vocabulary and the Well-Architected Framework
lessons.summary: What 99.9% really allows, composite SLAs, RPO and RTO, and the five pillars every design review should walk through.
objectives: Convert an SLA percentage into minutes of downtime
Work out a composite SLA for a chain of services
Name the five Well-Architected pillars and one question for each

lessons.title: Your first real workload on Azure
lessons.summary: A React app, a Node API and a SQL database - which services, what gets created, what it costs and what to do next.
objectives: Map a typical three-tier web app onto Azure services
Describe every resource that gets created and why
Estimate a monthly cost and know where the certification path goes next

modules.title: Compute and hosting
modules.tagline: Virtual machines, App Service, Static Web Apps, Functions, containers and AKS - and how to choose.
modules.description: Every way Azure can run your code, from a virtual machine you patch yourself to a function billed per execution. Each lesson names what the service is really for, what it costs, how it scales and what it cannot do - and the module ends with a decision guide you can run in a design review.

lessons.title: Virtual machines and scale sets
lessons.summary: Renting a computer: sizes and families, disks, images, availability sets and zones, and scaling out with VM Scale Sets.
objectives: Read a VM size name and say what family and generation it is
Choose between managed disk tiers and explain what they cost
Say when a virtual machine is the right answer and when it is an admission of defeat

lessons.title: App Service - the PaaS home for web apps and APIs
lessons.summary: The plan versus the app, pricing tiers, scaling rules, deployment slots and the settings that trip teams up.
objectives: Explain what an App Service plan is and why it is what you pay for
Pick a tier from the requirements for scale, slots, zones and networking
Use deployment slots for a zero-downtime release and know when a swap goes wrong

lessons.title: Static Web Apps for React and React Native web
lessons.summary: Global static hosting with a build pipeline, free certificates, staging environments and an optional managed API.
objectives: Describe how a React build gets from a Git push to a global edge
Decide between Static Web Apps, App Service and blob hosting for a front end
Use pull-request preview environments and the built-in authentication

lessons.title: Azure Functions and serverless thinking
lessons.summary: Triggers and bindings, the hosting plans, cold starts, and the workloads that serverless suits or ruins.
objectives: Name the common triggers and say which fits a given job
Choose between Consumption, Flex Consumption, Premium and App Service plans
Explain cold starts, timeouts and the cost curve that makes serverless expensive

lessons.title: Containers - Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps
lessons.summary: What a container buys you on Azure, where the image lives, and the three ways to run one without a cluster.
objectives: Say what a container changes about the shared responsibility line
Choose between Container Instances, Container Apps and App Service for containers
Describe how an image gets from a build to a running revision, and scale to zero

lessons.title: Azure Kubernetes Service - when you really need it
lessons.summary: What Kubernetes actually gives you, what AKS manages for you, the running costs, and the honest test for whether you need it.
objectives: Explain pods, nodes, node pools and the control plane in plain words
Say what AKS manages and what stays your job
Apply an honest test for whether a team should adopt Kubernetes

lessons.title: Choosing compute - a decision guide
lessons.summary: One flow chart, the questions behind it, cost shapes compared, and how to defend the answer in a design review.
objectives: Walk a workload through the compute decision tree and land on a service
Compare the cost shape of per-instance, per-execution and per-cluster billing
Argue a compute choice to a team, including when to revisit it

modules.title: Storage and data
modules.tagline: Storage accounts, Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Redis and picking the right store for the job.
modules.description: Where data lives on Azure and how to choose, written for a SQL Server professional: blobs, files, queues and tables in a storage account; Azure SQL in its three flavours; Cosmos DB for global scale; Redis for speed; PostgreSQL and MySQL; and backup you have actually restored from. Each store lesson names the data shape it suits, what it costs, how it scales and what breaks - and the module ends with a decision guide you can run in a design review.

lessons.title: Storage accounts - blobs, files, queues and tables
lessons.summary: One resource, four services: blobs, Files, queues and tables, with redundancy options, access tiers and the right way to let an app in.
objectives: Say which of the four storage services fits a given piece of data
Choose a redundancy option and an access tier, and know what archive really costs
Secure an account with managed identity and short-lived SAS instead of account keys

lessons.title: Azure SQL for the SQL Server professional
lessons.summary: SQL Database, Managed Instance or SQL Server on a VM; DTU versus vCore, the service tiers, and what your Always On knowledge becomes.
objectives: Choose between SQL Database, Managed Instance and SQL Server on a VM from the features an estate uses
Pick a purchasing model and service tier, and say when serverless or an elastic pool fits
Explain zone redundancy, active geo-replication and failover groups in availability-group terms

lessons.title: Cosmos DB - planet-scale NoSQL
lessons.summary: Request units, the partition key you cannot change, five consistency levels, multiple regions - and the honest test for whether you need it.
objectives: Say which data belongs in Cosmos DB and which should stay relational
Choose a partition key and recognise a hot partition from its 429s
Pick a consistency level and capacity mode, and explain what each extra region costs

lessons.title: Caching with Azure Cache for Redis
lessons.summary: Cache-aside, session state across scaled-out instances, the tiers and their SLAs, and the ways a cache shows customers data that is no longer true.
objectives: Apply the cache-aside pattern and choose a TTL a customer can live with
Move session state out of instance memory so the API can scale out
Pick a tier and eviction policy, and name what breaks when caches go wrong

lessons.title: Open-source databases - PostgreSQL and MySQL on Azure
lessons.summary: Flexible Server for PostgreSQL and MySQL: tiers, HA versus read replicas, connection pooling, extensions like pgvector, and the real cost of a second engine.
objectives: Explain what Flexible Server manages and what its tiers cost
Tell zone-redundant HA from a read replica and say what each is for
Decide whether a second database engine is worth what it adds to the team

lessons.title: Backup, recovery and data protection
lessons.summary: Why redundancy is not backup, what each data store protects by default, vaults and Site Recovery, and the restore drill that proves any of it works.
objectives: Tell redundancy from backup and match each to the threats it covers
State the default backup and retention for Azure SQL, Flexible Server, Cosmos DB and blobs
Run a restore drill and turn it into a measured RTO

lessons.title: Choosing a data store - a decision guide
lessons.summary: One decision tree, six questions in order, four cost shapes, and how to defend a data-store choice in a design review.
objectives: Walk new data through the six questions and land on a store
Compare per-GB, per-vCore, per-RU and per-cache-size billing for a workload
Argue a data-store choice to a team, including who owns it and when to revisit it

modules.title: Networking, identity and security
modules.tagline: Virtual networks, load balancing, private endpoints, Entra ID, RBAC, managed identities, Key Vault and Defender.
modules.description: The two things that make or break an Azure estate: how traffic flows and who is allowed to do what. Virtual networks and NSGs, the four ways to balance load, private endpoints and the DNS behind them, Entra ID, RBAC and managed identities, Key Vault, and Defender for Cloud - ending with zero trust and the whole shop walked through by an attacker.

lessons.title: Virtual networks, subnets and network security groups
lessons.summary: Address spaces and subnets, network security groups, Bastion instead of open RDP, peering, and when hub-and-spoke earns its cost.
objectives: Plan a non-overlapping address space and size subnets for the services that need them
Write NSG rules that deny by default, using service tags and priorities correctly
Say when one VNet is enough and when hub-and-spoke with a firewall is justified

lessons.title: Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door and Traffic Manager
lessons.summary: Layer 4 or layer 7, regional or global: which of the four to use, health probes that tell the truth, and locking the origin behind the WAF.
objectives: Choose between Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door and Traffic Manager from two questions
Design a health probe that moves traffic for the right reasons
Make sure a WAF cannot be bypassed and nothing personal is cached at the edge

lessons.title: Private endpoints, DNS and hybrid connectivity
lessons.summary: Private endpoints and the DNS that makes them work, service endpoints, reaching private names from the office, and VPN versus ExpressRoute.
objectives: Make a PaaS resource private with a private endpoint and close its public endpoint
Design private DNS zones so the cloud and the office resolve the same names
Choose between site-to-site VPN and ExpressRoute for a named requirement

lessons.title: Microsoft Entra ID - the identity backbone
lessons.summary: Identities, tokens and app registrations, MFA and Conditional Access, break-glass accounts, and why customers and contractors live somewhere else.
objectives: Explain how Entra ID signs users in and what an API must check in a token
Set up app registrations and app roles without secrets that expire at 3am
Choose MFA and Conditional Access settings, and where staff, contractors and customers sign in

lessons.title: Role-based access control and managed identities
lessons.summary: Principal, role and scope; control-plane versus data-plane roles; least privilege with PIM; managed identities and secret-free pipelines.
objectives: Read a role assignment as principal, role and scope, and predict what it allows
Grant data-plane roles to apps and remove standing Owner with PIM
Replace keys, passwords and client secrets with managed identities and workload identity federation

lessons.title: Key Vault, secrets and App Configuration
lessons.summary: What belongs in Key Vault and what in App Configuration, Key Vault references, soft delete and purge protection, rotation, and feature flags.
objectives: Decide which values are secrets, which are configuration, and which should not exist
Use Key Vault references, vault-per-environment and purge protection correctly
Plan secret rotation and use feature flags to release without a deploy

lessons.title: Defender for Cloud, Sentinel and the security baseline
lessons.summary: Prevent, assess, detect, respond: Azure Policy, Defender for Cloud and its secure score, Defender plans, and when Sentinel is worth running.
objectives: Match Azure Policy, Defender for Cloud, Defender plans and Sentinel to the jobs they do
Use the security benchmark and secure score to prioritise, and produce compliance evidence
Route alerts to people and decide when a SIEM is worth running

lessons.title: Zero trust and securing a web workload end to end
lessons.summary: Zero trust's three principles, defence in depth, the whole shop walked through by an attacker, threat modelling, and a minimum bar for every workload.
objectives: Explain zero trust and defence in depth, and spot designs that trust the network
Walk an attacker through a workload and name the control that stops each step
Run a threat model at a design review and hold every workload to a minimum bar

modules.title: Integration and messaging
modules.tagline: Service Bus, Event Grid, Event Hubs, API Management and Logic Apps - decoupling systems the Azure way.
modules.description: How systems talk to each other without being tied together: what must happen now and what can happen after; queues, topics, events and streams; Service Bus for business messages, Event Grid for reactions, Event Hubs for high-volume streams; API Management as one front door for every API; and Logic Apps for the glue - each with what it costs and what breaks.

lessons.title: Messaging patterns - queues, topics, events and streams
lessons.summary: What must happen now and what can happen after; messages, events and streams; queues, pub/sub, at-least-once delivery, and which Azure broker fits.
objectives: Decide which steps must be synchronous and which belong on a message
Tell messages, events and streams apart and pick the Azure service for each
Design consumers for at-least-once delivery, dead-lettering and eventual consistency

lessons.title: Service Bus - enterprise messaging
lessons.summary: Queues, topics and filtered subscriptions; peek-lock and the dead-letter queue; sessions, duplicate detection, the transactional outbox, and the tiers.
objectives: Design topics, subscriptions and filters, and receive messages safely with peek-lock
Own the dead-letter queue: alerts, investigation and resubmission
Use sessions, duplicate detection and the transactional outbox, and choose a tier

lessons.title: Event Grid - reacting to what happens
lessons.summary: Push instead of poll: system and custom topics, filtered subscriptions, retries and dead-lettering, webhooks to partners, and when Service Bus is the better home.
objectives: Replace polling with Event Grid system and custom topics
Configure event subscriptions with filters, retries and a dead-letter destination
Choose between Event Grid and Service Bus, and combine them when a reaction must not be lost

lessons.title: Event Hubs - high-volume streaming
lessons.summary: Streams as retained logs, partitions and keys, consumer groups and checkpoints, throughput units, Capture and Stream Analytics, and why clicks are not orders.
objectives: Tell a stream from a queue and decide when Event Hubs is the right home
Choose partitions, partition keys and consumer groups, and checkpoint safely
Get value from a stream with Capture, Stream Analytics and Functions

lessons.title: API Management - one front door for your APIs
lessons.summary: One gateway for every API: products, subscriptions and keys, policies for tokens and rate limits, versions, the developer portal, tiers, and where Front Door fits.
objectives: Explain what an API gateway does and design API Management products for different consumers
Write policies for token validation, rate limits and quotas, and keep business logic out of them
Lock backends to the gateway, version APIs, and choose a tier

lessons.title: Logic Apps and low-code integration
lessons.summary: Workflows, triggers and connectors; Consumption versus Standard; when low-code beats code and when it does not; and the engineering discipline low-code still needs.
objectives: Build integration glue as Logic Apps workflows with connectors instead of custom services
Choose between Logic Apps Consumption and Standard, Power Automate, Functions and Durable Functions
Run workflows with proper identity, secrets, error handling, source control and monitoring

modules.title: Observability and reliability
modules.tagline: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights, alerts, and designing for failure.
modules.description: Seeing what a system is doing and keeping it running: Azure Monitor and what it collects only if asked, Log Analytics and just enough KQL, Application Insights and distributed tracing, alerts that page on symptoms with SLOs and error budgets, high availability and disaster recovery patterns proven by drills, and the Well-Architected review that ties it together.

lessons.title: Azure Monitor - metrics, logs and the data platform
lessons.summary: Monitoring versus observability, metrics, logs, traces and changes, what Azure collects by itself and what you must switch on, and one workspace per environment.
objectives: Explain the signals behind observability and what each is good for
Switch on what Azure does not collect by default: diagnostic settings, the Monitor Agent and data collection rules
Design Log Analytics workspaces and enforce the logging baseline with policy

lessons.title: Log Analytics and just enough KQL
lessons.summary: The tables that matter, KQL for SQL Server people, five queries every team needs, workbooks, and the levers that cut a log bill by two thirds.
objectives: Read and write KQL queries using what you know from T-SQL
Build the team's incident queries and a workbook everyone opens first
Control log cost with collection choices, table plans, retention and commitment tiers

lessons.title: Application Insights for web apps and APIs
lessons.summary: Instrumenting APIs, React and React Native with OpenTelemetry and the JS SDK, distributed tracing end to end, the application map, availability tests, sampling and privacy.
objectives: Instrument servers, browsers and mobile apps so telemetry reaches one Application Insights resource
Follow one request end to end with distributed tracing and the application map

lessons.title: Alerts, action groups and on-call that works
lessons.summary: Alert rules and action groups, paging on symptoms not causes, SLIs, SLOs and error budgets, Service Health, and the habits that make on-call humane.
objectives: Build alert rules and action groups that page only when users are hurt

lessons.title: High availability and disaster recovery patterns
lessons.summary: RTO and RPO per capability, zones and resilient code, four cross-region strategies, failing over the whole stack, and proving it with drills, chaos and load tests.
objectives: Set RTO and RPO per business capability and choose a matching strategy
Apply retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead and degradation patterns within a region
Fail over the whole stack and prove it with DR drills, chaos experiments and load tests

lessons.title: The Well-Architected review in practice
lessons.summary: Reviewing one workload against the five pillars: Advisor triage, failure mode analysis, trade-offs recorded as decision records, and a short list of owned risks.
objectives: Scope and run a Well-Architected review of one workload with the team that runs it
Carry out failure mode analysis, including the risks you accept
Record trade-offs as architecture decision records and leave with owned, dated actions

modules.title: DevOps on Azure
modules.tagline: Azure DevOps and GitHub, pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and release strategies.
modules.description: Shipping software to Azure repeatably: DevOps as a way of working and the two toolchains, trunk-based branching with protected main, Azure Pipelines and GitHub Actions with federated identities, Bicep and Terraform with what-if and drift control, securing the software supply chain, release strategies that roll back in seconds, and the tests and DORA metrics that show whether it is all working.

lessons.title: DevOps on Azure - the landscape and the two toolchains
lessons.summary: What DevOps really is, CI and CD, the pipeline as the only way to production, and choosing between Azure DevOps and GitHub - or using both with clear jobs.
objectives: Explain DevOps, continuous integration and continuous delivery in practical terms
Compare Azure DevOps and GitHub and decide where each kind of work should live
Make the pipeline the only way to production

lessons.title: Repos, branching and pull-request policies
lessons.summary: Trunk-based development versus GitFlow, pull requests worth reviewing, branch policies and protection rules, CODEOWNERS, and semantic versions that say what is running.
objectives: Choose a branching strategy that fits how the software is deployed

lessons.title: Azure Pipelines - YAML, agents, stages and environments
lessons.summary: YAML pipelines with stages, jobs and steps, build once and deploy many, agents and pools, environments with approvals, federated service connections, and templates.
objectives: Write a YAML pipeline with stages, jobs and steps that builds once and deploys many times

lessons.title: GitHub Actions for Azure
lessons.summary: Workflows, jobs, runners and actions; OIDC sign-in bound to environments; protection rules; pinned actions and least-privilege tokens; and the map from Azure Pipelines.
objectives: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that builds once and deploys through environments

lessons.title: Infrastructure as code - Bicep and Terraform

objectives: Choose between Bicep and Terraform for a given estate
Structure infrastructure as modules, layers and per-environment parameters deployed by pipeline

lessons.title: Secrets, identities and security in the pipeline
lessons.summary: The pipeline as production's front door: no secrets, push protection, dependency and code scanning, SBOMs and signed provenance, and keeping credentials away from untrusted code.
objectives: Remove pipeline secrets with federation, managed identities and Key Vault, and respond to leaks

lessons.title: Release strategies - slots, blue-green, canary and feature flags
lessons.summary: Deploying versus releasing, rolling, blue-green, canary and ring-based releases, slot swaps and revisions, metric gates, and expand-and-contract for data.
objectives: Separate deploying from releasing and choose rolling, blue-green, canary or ring-based releases

lessons.title: Quality gates, testing and DevOps metrics
lessons.summary: The test pyramid with real dependencies, smoke tests and quality gates people trust, and the four DORA metrics that show whether delivery is improving.
objectives: Shape a test suite around the pyramid, using real dependencies where mocks would hide faults

modules.title: Azure AI
modules.tagline: Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, AI Services, AI Search, RAG, agents and responsible AI.
modules.description: The Azure AI platform at the level a lead needs: sorting AI ideas into buy, configure, prebuilt, generative and custom work; Azure OpenAI and Foundry Models with the right model and deployment type; Microsoft Foundry projects and the developer loop; prebuilt AI services with confidence thresholds; retrieval-augmented generation on Azure AI Search; agents that act with the user's permissions; responsible AI with layered safety and evaluation gates; and the gateway, security and operations that keep it affordable.

lessons.title: The Azure AI landscape
lessons.summary: Sorting "we need AI" into five kinds of work - buy, configure, prebuilt, generative and custom - the Azure AI stack behind them, and why nearly all of it is inference you pay for per call.
objectives: Sort AI ideas into buy, configure, prebuilt, generative and custom-model work
Describe the Azure AI stack: Foundry, Foundry Models, AI Services, AI Search and Azure Machine Learning
Explain inference and why an LLM call behaves like a stateless, non-deterministic function

lessons.title: Azure OpenAI and Foundry Models

lessons.title: Microsoft Foundry - projects, hubs and the developer loop
lessons.summary: The Foundry resource and its projects, hubs as the older model, connections and access, one resource per environment in its own subscription, and the loop from playground to code, evaluation, tracing and the pipeline.

lessons.title: Azure AI Services - vision, speech, language and documents

lessons.title: Azure AI Search and retrieval-augmented generation

lessons.title: Agents, tools and orchestration

lessons.title: Responsible AI, content safety and evaluation

lessons.title: Cost, security and operations for AI workloads
lessons.summary: Running AI like production: where token cost comes from and the levers that cut it, an AI gateway in API Management, identity, network and data security, and GenAIOps with model retirements and a kill switch.
objectives: Estimate and reduce cost per conversation with routing, trimming, caching, batch and PTUs
Put an AI gateway in front of every model call for limits, metering, caching and failover

modules.title: Architecture and leading a team

lessons.title: Reference architectures you will meet most

lessons.title: Certifications and how to keep learning

lessons.title: Capstone scenarios - design reviews you can run
